messages:
Sam Rivera: FYI - Nimbus Games reported an invoice line labeled `embedding-512 surge` for 2026-03-31 for ~1.2M tokens. Their dashboard shows ~120k for the same day. Can someone take a look?
Priya Patel: @Sam can you paste the account id + invoice id? initial thought: backfill double-count or delayed ingest.
Sam Rivera: account: ACCT-99873, invoice: INV-2026-03-99873. Customer says they touched nothing except a plan upgrade on 3/17.
Nico Alvarez: copying the customer's note: "We only upgraded to Growth on 3/17; our dashboard has steady usage. The invoice shows a sudden huge embedding charge 3/31 — we never hit that scale."
Jamie O'Neill: If the upgrade changed tier pricing mid-month, invoice could show different per-token rate, but that wouldn't cause 10x token count delta. sounds like duplicate events.
Priya Patel: digging into ledger: found two metering events for 2026-03-31 01:05Z for the same model+customer with identical token_count=1,080,000. One event has source="ingest" (request_id=req-7f4a), the other has source="backfill" (request_id=null). Both marked chargeable=true.
Priya Patel: SQL I ran to surface duplicates:```sql
SELECT account_id, model, usage_day, SUM(token_count) as billed_tokens, COUNT(*) as rows
FROM metering.ledger
WHERE account_id = 'ACCT-99873' AND usage_day = '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY account_id, model, usage_day
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
```
Sam Rivera: BillingBot showed a scheduled backfill job on 2026-03-31 01:00Z for embeddings retention migration.
BillingBot: Scheduled job executed: backfill/emb-retention v2 — run_id=run-20260331-01-05 — status: finished — entries_written=1,200,342.
Priya Patel: looks like the backfill inserted rows without request_id/idempotency keys, so the metering ingest and the backfill both created chargeable records. Patch needed in backfill to set request_id and set `backfill=true` so the billing pipeline dedupes by (request_id || backfill_marker).
Priya Patel: repro steps for eng to validate and fix: 1) find accounts where billed_tokens / dashboard_tokens > 5 for a single day 2) check metering.ledger rows for that day for duplicate model+usage_day 3) inspect metering_worker logs for "backfill: true" and missing request_id 4) run reconcile script to mark backfill rows as non-chargeable if duplicate. Example query to find candidates:```sql
SELECT l.* FROM metering.ledger l
LEFT JOIN dashboard.daily_tokens d ON d.account_id = l.account_id AND d.usage_day = l.usage_day
WHERE d.dashboard_tokens <  (l.token_count * 0.2)
AND l.usage_day = '2026-03-31'
AND l.account_id = 'ACCT-99873';
```
Priya Patel: mitigation plan: 1) run reconcile to identify duplicated backfill rows and set chargeable=false for the backfill copy 2) issue an invoice credit for the duplicated tokens 3) patch backfill code to emit `request_id` and `backfill_marker` and add idempotency guard 4) add an alert to billing-runbook for anomalous daily ratio > 3x between billed and dashboard.
Jamie O'Neill: can finance draft the credit amount? if we credit ~1,000,000 tokens at $0.0003/token that's $300. also confirm tier change pricing didn't exacerbate cost.
Priya Patel: I prepared a quick reconcile script. Command to preview duplicates:```bash
./scripts/reconcile_backfill_duplicates --account ACCT-99873 --day 2026-03-31 --preview
```
Priya Patel: applied preview -> found backfill rows with null request_id; reconcile would mark 1,028,000 tokens as non-chargeable.
Sam Rivera: Per customer impact, Nico — can you draft a message offering immediate credit and explaining root cause + ETA for permanent fix? keep it simple.
Nico Alvarez: Draft: "Hi team — we found a duplicate billing entry created by a scheduled internal backfill that re-ingested usage without an idempotency key. We've applied a credit for the duplicated tokens and are shipping a patch so this doesn't recur. Sorry for the noise; we'll follow up with details and the credit on your next invoice." want to include amount?
Jamie O'Neill: include the credit amount and when they'll see it on invoice. approve $310 to be safe (covers price variance).
Priya Patel: technical fix PR created: https://redwood.internal/pulls/5821 — PR summary: set request_id on backfill rows, add unique index on (account_id, model, usage_day, request_id, backfill_marker) to prevent duplicates; tests added. commit: d9f7c3b.
Priya Patel: I've run the reconcile in preview; if finance approves I'll flip to execute which will mark 1,028,000 tokens as non-chargeable and emit a credit invoice line.
Jamie O'Neill: finance approves. please run reconcile and create credit memo for INV-2026-03-99873.
Priya Patel: reconcile executed @1764015200 — marked backfill duplicates non-chargeable, created credit memo CM-2026-03-99873 amount $310.
BillingBot: Credit memo created: CM-2026-03-99873 — amount $310 — applied to invoice INV-2026-03-99873.
Nico Alvarez: I just notified the customer and included the PR link + credit memo id. customer replied: "Thanks for the quick turnaround — appreciate the transparency and the fix." :relieved: 
Sam Rivera: closing this thread — root cause: backfill lacked idempotency keys and created duplicate chargeable ledger rows. action items: patch deployed (PR 5821), alert added to runbook, reconcile tool improved. :white_check_mark:
